items.title: send this prompt to claude tonight... it interviews you until it knows your business
items.summary:
send this prompt to claude tonight... it interviews you until it knows your business

an agent that doesn't know your business writes like a stranger. this prompt fixes that in one sitting

paste it into claude or codex. if typing is slow, answer out loud with a dictation tool

the prompt ↓

"you're going to interview me to build my company brain, a folder of plain files every ai agent in my company reads before it works

rules
​> one question at a time, wait for my answer
​> ask for real examples, not descriptions. "paste your last won proposal" beats "describe your proposals"
​> when an answer is vague, ask one follow-up before moving on
​> never fill a gap with a guess, write [ask owner] instead

cover these in order, and write each file as soon as its section is done
1. company .md, what we do, for whom, what we do differently
2. clients .md, who buys, who signs, what triggers the purchase, their exact words
3. offer .md, every service, what's in scope, what costs extra
4. pricing-rules .md, how we price, our minimums, what we never discount
5. no-list .md, the clients, deals and terms we turn down, and why
6. objections .md, the pushback we hear on calls and how we answer it
7. voice .md, 3 emails i wrote that worked, and the words we never use

when you're done, list every [ask owner] gap and the file it belongs to"

the first draft will have gaps. that's what [ask owner] is for, you see exactly what's missing instead of a confident guess

do sections 1 and 5 first

items.title: Ever read a PR description from your coding agent three times and still not know what changed? Zonder Labs wrote up why
items.summary:
Ever read a PR description from your coding agent three times and still not know what changed? Zonder Labs wrote up why AI writing at work is so tiring to read, and it's a good checklist.

They hand-labeled AI and human samples, from articles to Claude Code replies and Stack Overflow answers, and sorted the unclear sentences into three faults:

1. Hidden actors and actions. "A request for grapes was made upon the duck's arrival" hides who did what. Name the actor and use the verb.
2. Vague wording, the most common fault in Claude Code. Their real example: "The database readiness check sits at the user-session entry boundary, before the authentication handler runs."
3. Empty statements and misplaced emphasis, where you understand every word and still can't find the point.

They also compared their labels with AI detectors. The words people hunt for, like "delve" and em dashes, say little about whether a reader can follow the text.

Worth pasting into your agent's rules as a check for its own PR descriptions and summaries

items.title: @carldraper @nicoloboschi Same lesson here. Mixing every repo and a personal agent into one bank turns recall into a sea
items.summary: @carldraper @nicoloboschi Same lesson here. Mixing every repo and a personal agent into one bank turns recall into a search through old timestamps. What helped us was one store per repo, plus marking an old decision replaced when a new one lands, so recall stops returning both.
